source.textual_sequence: ... jri̯ ḥnn Šw ... sḫpr kꜣ.t Tfn.wt
source.translation_summary: the phallus of Shu ... the vulva of Tefnut

comparison.PT685: ḥnn + kꜣ.t in a generative/cosmogonic parallelism
comparison.pJumilhac_XVI16: ḥnn + kꜣ.t + mḥ in a sexual-retention episode
comparison.pBrooklyn_XI11: kꜣ.t + bjꜣ near Djed and phallus context
comparison.result: The female lexeme kꜣ.t and the male lexeme ḥnn have a substantially older attestation together than the Ptolemaic Jumilhac episode. This supports lexical continuity but not ritual or mechanical continuity.

topa_implication: Treat kꜣ.t and ḥnn as ancient lexical anchors. Search later corpora for added operators (mḥ, ḫfꜥ, insertion/withdrawal verbs) and material qualifiers (bjꜣ) rather than assuming a single frozen phrase.
